This page summarizes the main spectral and combinatorial phenomena from the dissertation alongside the computational verifications in [`docs/verifications.md`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/docs/verifications.md).

## Bipartite Spectral Non-Minimality (Theorem 1.7 / Example 3.33)

In classical Coxeter systems, bipartite Coxeter elements always minimize the spectral radius among all principal elements. In the 6-node bipartite mixed-sign graph `example_3_33`, the **bipartite** principal element has a strictly *larger* spectral radius than the linear principal element:

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../src")
sys.path.insert(0, "src")

from mixed_sign_coxeter import MixedSignCoxeterGraph

g = MixedSignCoxeterGraph.example_3_33()
rho_lin = g.spectral_radius([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
rho_bp = g.spectral_radius([0, 3, 5, 1, 2, 4])
print(f"Bipartite graph: {g.is_bipartite()}")
print(f"Linear principal element   [1,2,3,4,5,6]: rho = {rho_lin:.5f}")
print(f"Bipartite principal element [1,4,6,2,3,5]: rho = {rho_bp:.5f}")
```

## Non-Monotonicity of $\Lambda$ (Remark 3.30)

Adding a positive node along $A_2(+,-) \subset A_3(-,+,+) \subset A_4(-,+,+,+) \subset A_5(-,+,+,+,+)$ causes the minimal spectral radius $\Lambda$ to oscillate instead of increasing monotonically:

```{python}
from mixed_sign_coxeter import MixedSignCoxeterGraph

chain = [
    ("A2(+,-)",       ["+", "-"]),
    ("A3(-,+,+)",     ["-", "+", "+"]),
    ("A4(-,+,+,+)",   ["-", "+", "+", "+"]),
    ("A5(-,+,+,+,+)", ["-", "+", "+", "+", "+"]),
]
for label, signs in chain:
    lam, _ = MixedSignCoxeterGraph.A_n(signs).minimal_spectral_radius()
    print(f"{label:15s}  Lambda = {lam:.5f}")
```

## Computational Verifications Beyond the Dissertation

Full derivations and tests live in [`docs/verifications.md`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/docs/verifications.md) and `tests/test_verifications.py`:

1. **$W(\widetilde{A_{-n}}) \cong W(D_{n+1})$ for every even $n$** ([`isomorphisms.py`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/src/mixed_sign_coxeter/isomorphisms.py)): An explicit integer matrix $T$ of $D_{n+1}$ roots satisfies $T^T T = -B(\widetilde{A_{-n}})$ and conjugates $W(\widetilde{A_{-n}})$ onto $W(D_{n+1})$ of order $2^n (n+1)!$. For odd $n$, the cycle is bipartite and $W(\widetilde{A_{-n}})$ is infinite.
2. **Appendix D in Python**: Reproduces the GAP session for $W(\widetilde{A_{-4}})$, verifies all 16 relators, and proves faithfulness of order $1920$ via Todd–Coxeter enumeration.
3. **Remark A.3 (Table A.2 completeness)** ([`finite_search.py`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/src/mixed_sign_coxeter/finite_search.py)): Exhaustive search finds 4 additional finite rank-3 graphs and 24 additional finite rank-4 graphs beyond Table A.2 and Figure A.1 (all negative and non-bipartite).
4. **Question 3.35** ([`principal_search.py`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/src/mixed_sign_coxeter/principal_search.py)): Across 4,026 simply-laced cyclic graphs on 4–6 nodes, the smallest counterexample where the bipartite element fails to minimize is the alternating 4-cycle $(+,-,+,-)$ (formally verified in `AlternatingSquare.lean`).
5. **Question 2.59 & Single-Defect Cycles** ([`OddCycleSingleDefect.lean`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/lean/MixedSignCoxeter/OddCycleSingleDefect.lean), [`EvenCycleSingleDefect.lean`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/mixed.sign.coxeter.systems/blob/main/lean/MixedSignCoxeter/EvenCycleSingleDefect.lean)): On $C_6(+,-,+,-,+,-)$, distinct circulations $|c| \in \{0, 2, 4\}$ separate $\rho(w)$ ($5.82843$, $4.91314$, $8.18570$). Conversely, single-defect cycles exhibit a sharp parity dichotomy: for every odd cycle $C_{2m+1}(+,-,\dots,-)$ ($m \ge 1$), $(w+I)^2(w^{2m}-I)=0$ and $\rho(w) = 1$, whereas for every even cycle $C_{2m}(+,-,\dots,-)$ ($m \ge 2$), $w$ has a real eigenvalue $\lambda \in (-5, -1)$ and hence $\rho(w) > 1$.
